messages:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: SEV2 - inference-serving error-rate spike (rule: inference-5xx-high). Triggered for service=redwood-inference-prod, region=us-west-2. Incident ID: INC-2210-11. Pager: @sam @nikita oncall.

sam: acked on pagerduty, taking it. jumping in now. starting with top-level metrics.

nikita: +1 i was just about to check dashboards, will standby if you want me to take handoff shortly (i'm wrapping a client call).

sam: ok quick notes: 5xx rate up from 0.2% -> ~8% over last 3m, spike concentrated on /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings. latency also up ~70ms p50 -> 350ms on some hosts. traces show a bunch of `kv-cache` timeouts and grpc connect failures to runtime pods.

jordan: @sam can you paste the svc and pod list? i can look at infra side (autoscaler/nebula).

sam: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference -o wide`
```
NAME                                READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE     IP
inference-9bf4c6d7-0us2  2/2     Running   0          12d    10.2.3.45
inference-9bf4c6d7-1kz8  2/2     Running   0          12d    10.2.3.46
inference-9bf4c6d7-2mp4  1/2     CrashLoop 5          1h     10.2.3.58
inference-9bf4c6d7-3qz1  2/2     Running   0          12d    10.2.3.59
```

sam: see `2mp4` is crashing, logs show repeated `rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = context deadline exceeded` and `failed to load kv shard` errors.

leah: i'm on the trace UI. those crashing pods are all hitting the same model shard leader. could be a degraded GPU on node ip 10.3.12.7.

matt: i see that node in cloud console showing `NVIDIA driver lost` around 08:12:14 UTC. kernel logged an oops and kubelet restarted the container.

nikita: hmm that would explain kv-cache leader flips causing RPC timeouts. if leader keeps moving, clients will see 5xx.

sam: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node 10.3.12.7 2) drain pods from that node, 3) trigger a hot-restart for the affected inference pods to force reconnections to new shard leader, 4) if still failing, fallback route on the router to model-variant-quantized (lower perf, healthier).

jordan: i'll cordon/drain. running: `gcloud compute instances set-scheduling node-123 --maintenance-policy=terminate` (we prefer to force eviction for a bad GPU).

pagerbot: Action logged: node cordon requested by jordan at 08:18:02 UTC.

sam: doing a rolling restart of inference deployment now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference -n inference` — this will restart replicas not on the cordoned node.

leah: rerouting rule ready: `traffic-route: if error_rate>1% -> model=redwood-mini-quant` — can flip manually if errors persist.

matt: cordon completed, drain in progress. first drained pod terminated with grace 30s, second interrupted and evicted.

sam: watch logs on the restarted pods. tailing one: `kubectl logs -n inference inference-9bf4c6d7-7xy2 -c runtime -f`
```
[08:20:35 UTC] runtime: connected to kv-leader shard-7 (10.2.5.3)
[08:20:36 UTC] runtime: warm cache hits rising, tail-latency normalizing
[08:20:37 UTC] runtime: request handled, 200 OK
```

sam: getting 200s again on that host. overall 5xx rate dropped to ~0.6% in next 2m. still above baseline but trending down.

nikita: i'm going to ack rotation duty — i'm taking the active incident owner from sam at 08:22. Sam, please handoff any outstanding next steps.

sam: handing off. outstanding: watch for resurgence for next 20-30m, if 5xx > 1% for 3m escalate to fallback routing; prepare a temporary rollout of model-variant-quantized if errors persist; optional: file a host hardware ticket for node-123 GPU. i updated the incident notes in INC-2210-11.

nikita: got it. i'll stand watch. also pinging infra-ops to open a hardware ticket: `infra-ops@redwood` — can someone please file?

jordan: filed ticket HW-2210-17, referenced node-123 and attached kernel oops logs. ETA hardware triage 2h.

pagerbot: PagerDuty: ownership updated to nikita at 08:22:41 UTC. Incident remains SEV2.

leah: customer-impact: found a spike in /embeddings failures affecting ~4% of requests for a subset of API keys (high-volume partners). I exported a quick CSV of keys and sample errors and uploaded to the incident doc. recommending outreach if thresholds exceeded after 30m.

nikita: thanks — i'll watch partner error rates and coordinate comms if they stay degraded. also setting a temporary alert: `alert: embeddings-partner-5xx -> notify #oncall, owners` with a 10m evaluation window.

sam: great. small note: if this resurfaces and we need immediate low-latency fallback, flip `traffic-route` now. i'll be reachable if needed.

matt: cloud autoscaler recorded a temporary spike in pod restarts; we should check if HPA needs new thresholds. opening a follow-up task.

nikita: update at 08:34 UTC: error rate back to 0.3% for 10m window. partner errors trending down too. keeping oncall watch for another 20m then will close incident if stable.

pagerbot: Incident INC-2210-11 updated: owner=nikita, status=monitoring, last_update=08:34:12 UTC.

jordan: thumbs on infra side. thanks all for quick moves.

sam: thanks team — handoff complete.

nikita: 08:52 UTC — still stable, no further 5xx spikes. i'll close the PD incident after a 30m quiet window.

pagerbot: PagerDuty: incident INC-2210-11 set to resolved by nikita at 09:22:41 UTC (resolution reason: transient GPU/node failure; pods restarted; fallback not required).

nikita: note for postmortem: hardware failure on node-123 caused kv-cache leader instability leading to RPC timeouts. remediation: add node health probe for GPU driver, reduce KV leader shard concentration, and add automated router fallback after 2m of elevated 5xx. assigning follow-ups to eng-infra.
